landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest (Alpine Lakes Wilderness)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass / National Park Pass
drive: From the Deception Pass Trailhead

landManager: National Park Service — North Cascades National Park (Stephen Mather Wilderness)
storedPass: None — the Thornton Lakes Trailhead lies inside North Cascades National Park, so no Northwest Forest Pass or NPS entrance fee applies; only the overnight wilderness permit above is required.
drive: Start at the Thornton Lakes Trailhead (~2,500 ft), reached via the rough spur road off SR-20 near milepost 117.

landManager: U.S. Forest Service — Olympic National Forest, Hood Canal Ranger District (Mount Skokomish Wilderness)
storedPass: $5/vehicle day-use fee or $30 annual Northwest Forest Pass required to park at the upper trailhead — Interagency/Digital Pass also accepted (cash not accepted on site); the lower trailhead is fee-free.
drive: From the Upper Trailhead (elev. ~3,500 ft, at the end of FS Road 2419-014 off FS 24/FS 2419 - the lot has a vault toilet, picnic table, and requires a Northwest Forest Pass), Trail #812 climbs immediately.

landManager: North Cascades National Park Service Complex (NPS)
Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Mt. Baker Ranger District) — Mount Baker Wilderness, with some upper routes crossing into North Cascades National Park
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass required at most trailheads — $30/year or $5/day.
drive: Start from the Bagley Lakes Trailhead (~4,200 ft) at the south end of the upper Mt. Baker Ski Area parking lot near the Heather Meadows Visitor Center.

names: North Fork Quinault Trailhead / Ranger Station
landManager: National Park Service — Olympic National Park (Olympic Wilderness)
storedPass: Olympic NP entrance fee: $30/vehicle (7-day), $55 annual Olympic NP pass, or $80 America the Beautiful interagency annual pass.
drive: From US-101 at milepost 126, turn onto South Shore Road and follow it 12.9 miles to the Quinault River bridge; cross it, turn right onto North Shore Road, and drive 3.5 miles to the road end at the trailhead and ranger station.

landManager: National Park Service — Olympic National Park (Olympic Wilderness)
storedPass: None required at the Upper South Fork Skokomish trailhead, and there is no Olympic National Park entrance station on this approach.

landManager: Olympic National Forest (Hood Canal Ranger District), Mount Skokomish Wilderness
storedPass: No day-use fee at the Jefferson Creek/Jefferson Lake trailhead; a Northwest Forest Pass may be requested at some other nearby Olympic NF trailheads.
drive: From Hoodsport, drive about 14 miles north on US 101 to Hamma Hamma River Road (FR 25); follow it roughly 6.5 miles to FR 2480, then FR 2480 about 3 miles to FR 2401, then FR 2401 roughly 7-7.5 miles to the Jefferson Creek crossing / Jefferson Lake Trailhead area (~2,440 ft).

names: FR-6220 / Anderson Creek drainage (no maintained trail)
landManager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Skykomish Ranger District)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass or America the Beautiful pass required at developed trailheads.

names: FR-62 road-end (~2,800 ft, off US-2 near Index)
landManager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Skykomish Ranger District)
storedPass: No federal pass needed at the FR-62 road-end pullout; the Hampton Resources recreation permit is what this approach requires.
drive: From US-2 near Index onto FR-62: left at both junctions, ~5 miles to the rough road-end and the West Ridge boot path

landManager: Mount Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Darrington Ranger District)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass / Interagency Pass
drive: From the Verlot Public Service Center on the Mountain Loop Highway, continue east about 4.6 miles and turn right onto Forest Road 4020 (Schweitzer Creek Road, signed for Boardman Lake/Ashland Lakes/Bear-Pinnacle Lake).

landManager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Darrington Ranger District)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass required at Mountain Loop Highway trailheads — $5/day or $30/year.
drive: From Granite Falls, take Quarry Road about 4 miles to the Mountain Loop Highway, turn left and go 10 miles to Verlot, continue 1 mile and turn right onto Mount Pilchuck Road, then follow FR-42 for 6.8 miles to the trailhead lot.

landManager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Darrington Ranger District)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass required at Mountain Loop Highway trailheads — $5/day or $30/year.
drive: From Darrington, turn right onto the Mountain Loop Highway and drive 12.5 miles to the signed turnoff on the left, then turn left onto FR-2095 and go 1.5 miles to the trailhead on the right.

landManager: National Park Service — Olympic National Park (Olympic Wilderness)
storedPass: Olympic NP entrance fee: $30/vehicle (7-day), $55 annual Olympic NP pass, or $80 America the Beautiful interagency annual pass.
drive: Via the Elwha Valley: Olympic Hot Springs Road is closed to vehicles at Madison Falls — walk or bike ~6-7 miles to the Whiskey Bend Trailhead

names: Ruth Creek Road pullout near milepost 3 (FS 32)
landManager: Mount Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest, Mt. Baker Ranger District (Mount Baker Wilderness)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass or Interagency Pass
drive: From a pullout near milepost 3 on Ruth Creek Road, just past a creek flowing over a concrete weir (~2,950 ft), off Hannegan Pass Road (FS 32) from the Mt. Baker Highway

names: White Salmon Road (hairpin) TH / Lower White Salmon Lodge
landManager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (approach) / National Park Service — North Cascades NP (upper mountain and summit)
storedPass: None required at the White Salmon Road pull-off; parking is very limited
drive: From the lower White Salmon lodge on SR-542 (White Salmon Road, FR-3075), via the old road into the White Salmon Creek drainage

names: White Salmon Lodge road gate (Mount Baker Highway hairpin)
landManager: National Park Service
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass
drive: At the hairpin on the Mount Baker Highway near mile 52, below the ski area, park in the small pull-off at the gated road to White Salmon Lodge. Don't block the gate.

landManager: U.S. Forest Service — Mount St. Helens National Volcanic Monument (Gifford Pinchot National Forest)
storedPass: $5/day/vehicle at Climber’s Bivouac, waived on the date of your climb with a valid climbing permit; any other day or night parked there needs the day fee or a Northwest Forest or Interagency pass.
drive: From the Climbers Bivouac trailhead (3,700 ft, the highest vehicle access on this side of the mountain, reached via FR-90/FR-83/FR-81/FR-830 from Cougar), the route starts on the signed Ptarmigan Trail #216A through open forest.

landManager: U.S. Forest Service — Mount St. Helens National Volcanic Monument (Gifford Pinchot National Forest)
storedPass: Washington Sno-Park permit to park at Marble Mountain Sno-Park during the winter Sno-Park season.
drive: From Cougar, drive east on Lewis River Road, which becomes Forest Road 90, to the junction with Forest Road 83; turn left and go about 6 miles to the Marble Mountain Sno-Park. Forest Road 83 is gated at the sno-park in winter and early spring.

landManager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Skykomish Ranger District)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass required at Mountain Loop Highway trailheads — $5/day or $30/year.
drive: From the Olney Creek Road gate

names: Hoh Rain Forest Visitor Center / Hoh River Trailhead
landManager: National Park Service — Olympic National Park (Olympic Wilderness)
storedPass: Olympic NP entrance fee: $30/vehicle (7-day), $55 annual Olympic NP pass, or $80 America the Beautiful interagency annual pass.
drive: From Forks, drive US-101 south about 13 miles and turn east onto Upper Hoh Road. Follow it about 18 miles to the visitor center and trailhead at the end of the road.

landManager: USDA Forest Service — Olympic National Forest (Buckhorn Wilderness)
storedPass: No fees; no Northwest Forest Pass or Discover Pass needed at either trailhead.
drive: Start at the Mt. Townsend Upper Trailhead (elev. ~3,300 ft), reached via Forest Road 27 off Penny Creek Road out of Quilcene - the trailhead has a small gravel lot and a Buckhorn Wilderness boundary sign where Trail #839 begins.

landManager: Olympic National Forest (Hood Canal Ranger District), Mount Skokomish Wilderness
Olympic National Forest — Buckhorn Wilderness, Hood Canal (Quilcene) Ranger District
storedPass: None required.
drive: Start at the Tubal Cain Trailhead (elev. ~3,300 ft, reached via FR 2870/2880), and follow the Tubal Cain Trail #840 (Copper Creek drainage) south.

landManager: Mount Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest, Mt. Baker Ranger District
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass required at the Cascade River Road trailhead/parking area
drive: Park at the Cascade River Road washout roughly 14.2 miles from Marblemount, about 100 yards past the Cascade River crossing near the FR 1570 junction (signed for Kindy Ridge/Found Lake).

landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, Cle Elum Ranger District.
drive: Start at the Stafford Creek Trailhead (Trail #1359), Cle Elum Ranger District, Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, at the end of Stafford Creek Road (FR 9703), which leaves North Fork Teanaway River Road (FR 9737) past 29 Pines Campground - a small, often-overflowing lot for roughly 20 cars (Northwest Forest Pass required).

names: NF-9070 road-end below Silver Basin (Hyak, I-90 Exit 54)
landManager: USDA Forest Service — FR-9070 runs through the Cle Elum Ranger District, Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass / America the Beautiful Pass (required at the FR-9070 PCT-crossing trailhead)
drive: From I-90 Exit 54 via Hyak Drive and NF-9070 (left fork at Ollallie Meadow) to the road-end turnaround

storedPass: N/A
drive: Drive to Tiffany Springs Campground (elev. ~6,760 ft) via Forest Road 39, accessed either from Conconully (south, via FR-37) or from Winthrop (southwest, via East Chewuch Road and FR-37) - both are long gravel-road drives of an hour or more.

landManager: Gifford Pinchot National Forest (Cowlitz Valley Ranger District) — Goat Rocks Wilderness
storedPass: Required at both the Snowgrass Flat and Berry Patch trailheads — $5/day or $30/year Northwest Forest Pass.
drive: From the Snowgrass Flats Trailhead (end of FR-2150, elev. ~4,600 ft), start on Trail 96 (Snowgrass Flat Trail).

landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, Methow Valley Ranger District — Lake Chelan-Sawtooth Wilderness
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass or Interagency Recreation Pass (or pay the $5 day-use fee)
drive: Park at the Eagle Creek/Oval trailhead (~3,000 ft) at the end of FR 4420-080, reached via Twisp River Road/FR 44 (~12.5 mi west of Twisp) and the West Buttermilk/FR 4420 spur.
